2	
3	Reviewer: PIXL (agent). Date: 2026-09-11.
4	Inputs: `reference.png` (sha256 d997cade…), `reference-b.png` (sha256 e76b40ce…).

11

13	
14	Both files are 32×32 with zero fractional-alpha pixels and an **identical
15	silhouette**: the same 390 opaque cells, bounding box x7–24, y3–27, an occupied
16	area of 18×25.
17

19	substitution: navy `#25354A` in `reference.png` where `reference-b.png` has

21	`#F4DDA2` marks, not alpha.
22	
23	So the disagreement is purely outline treatment, exactly as stated:
24	
25	| | `reference.png` | `reference-b.png` |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| Outline | continuous dark rim | none |
28	| Visible colors | 3 | 2 |
29	| Navy pixels | 180 (46.2% of the silhouette) | 0 |
30	| Interior fill left | 210 cells | 390 cells |
31

33	
34	Peeling the silhouette boundary ring by ring:
35	
36	| Depth from edge | Cells in ring | Navy cells |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| 1 | 92 | 92 |
39	| 2 | 82 | 82 |
40	| 3 | 58 | 6 |
41	| 4+ | 158 | 0 |
42	
43	The rim is a uniform **2-pixel** outline, plus 6 stray navy cells at depth 3 in
44	the inner corners of the head notch. A 1-pixel rim on the same silhouette would
45	be 92 cells (23.6%) and would leave 298 interior cells instead of 210.
46	
47	This matters more than it looks: a 2px outline on a figure this size spends
48	**46% of the character's pixels on its own edge**. Those are the pixels that
49	would otherwise carry the scout/medic distinction.
50	
51	## 3. Visual comparison — contact sheet
52	
53	`work/study/contact-sheet.png` shows three treatments (rows) on light, dark and
54	busy checkered grounds (columns), each at native scale, ×4 and ×8:
55	
56	1. `variant-as_supplied_2px_outline.png` — `reference.png` unmodified
57	2. `variant-as_supplied_no_outline.png` — `reference-b.png` unmodified
58	3. `variant-derived_1px_outline.png` — **agent-derived study material**: the
59	   same silhouette with the navy reduced to the single outermost ring. This is
60	   a third option offered for the decision, not an approved project style.
61	
62	Inspected at ×8 by the agent, on the three grounds:
63	
64	- **2px outline, dark ground**: the navy rim is close in value to the dark
65	  ground and the outer edge stops reading as an edge. The figure loses its
66	  silhouette boundary and reads as a teal block sitting in a dark well. This is
67	  the weakest cell in the sheet.
68	- **2px outline, light and busy grounds**: strong separation; the rim does its
69	  job. But the teal interior is visibly squeezed — on the ears/horns the navy
70	  closes over the form entirely and they read as solid dark shapes rather than
71	  outlined ones.
72	- **No outline, dark and light grounds**: clean and confident; the flat teal
73	  holds its shape well at every scale.
74	- **No outline, busy ground**: still separates, but the boundary is soft
75	  against similar-value clutter. This is the weakest cell for this treatment.
76	- **1px outline, all three grounds**: reads on every ground, keeps the outer
77	  boundary crisp on the busy ground, and preserves 298 interior cells. At ×8
78	  the ears/horns stay open shapes instead of filling in.
79

82	game's actual display scale**, which is itself unrecorded — see §5.

91	|---|---|---|---|

93	| 24 | 20 | 20.0% | 10.0% |
94	| 32 | 26 | 15.4% | 7.7% |
95	| 48 | 39 | 10.3% | 5.1% |
96	| 64 | 52 | 7.7% | 3.8% |
97	
98	Read as a constraint rather than a ranking: **a 2px outline is not viable below
99	roughly 48px of canvas** for two characters that must be told apart, because
100	below that the rim plus a side-view head leaves too few interior cells for a
101	satchel, a cross marking, a scope or a pose difference. A 1px outline is
102	comfortable from 24px up. No outline imposes no floor at all.
103	
104	## 5. What still has to come from the project owner
105	
106	Ranked by how much they block work:
107	
108	1. **`edge_treatment`** — conflict. Choose one of: 2px rim as in
109	   `reference.png`; no rim as in `reference-b.png`; or the 1px middle option in
110	   row 3. Everything raster is blocked on this.
111	2. **`px`** — unresolved. Both references are 32×32 with an 18×25 occupancy,
112	   which is evidence of intent but not a stated decision. If the 2px rim is
113	   chosen, §4 argues for 48×48.
114	3. **`display_scale`** — unresolved and not in the brief. §3 shows the outline
115	   decision is invisible at 1× and obvious at 8×. Knowing the intended on-screen
116	   scale would make choice 1 much easier to settle.
117	4. **`engine`** — unresolved and not in the brief. Engine acceptance for the
118	   family cannot be planned, let alone verified, until a destination exists.
119	
120	## 6. Agent recommendation (not a decision)
121	
122	**1px outline at 32×32**, on this evidence: it is the only treatment that reads
123	on all three grounds at every inspected scale (§3), it returns 88 interior
124	cells to the character compared with the supplied 2px rim (§2), and it keeps
125	the navy `#25354A` that `reference.png` introduces rather than discarding a
126	color the owner may have chosen deliberately. It is also the option that stays
127	viable if the canvas later moves down to 24px.
128	
129	If the busy-ground case is not real for this game — flat or high-contrast
130	backgrounds only — then `reference-b.png`'s no-outline treatment is the better
131	answer and the simpler contract, and 32×32 still holds.
132	
133	The 2px rim as supplied is the one option this study argues against at 32×32,
134	purely on the interior-budget arithmetic in §2 and §4. It becomes reasonable
135	again at 48×48.
136	
137	## 7. Limits of this study
138	
139	- Measurements in §1, §2 and §4 are computed from the actual supplied files and
140	  are reproducible with `work/tools/edge_study.py`.
141	- §3 is the agent's visual inspection of the contact sheet. It is not the
142	  project owner's judgment and does not settle a conflicting choice.
143	- The references are blocky placeholder forms, not characters. Conclusions
144	  about interior budget are arithmetic about cell counts; they are not
145	  validated against an actual scout or medic pose, because none exists yet.
146	- Nothing here was generated by PixelLab. No remote generation tool was
147	  available in this session.

color the owner may have chosen deliberately. It is also the option that stays
viable if the canvas later moves down to 24px.

backgrounds only — then `reference-b.png`'s no-outline treatment is the better
answer and the simpler contract, and 32×32 still holds.

The 2px rim as supplied is the one option this study argues against at 32×32,
purely on the interior-budget arithmetic in §2 and §4. It becomes reasonable
again at 48×48.

- Measurements in §1, §2 and §4 are computed from the actual supplied files and
  are reproducible with `work/tools/edge_study.py`.
- §3 is the agent's visual inspection of the contact sheet. It is not the
  project owner's judgment and does not settle a conflicting choice.
- The references are blocky placeholder forms, not characters. Conclusions
  about interior budget are arithmetic about cell counts; they are not
  validated against an actual scout or medic pose, because none exists yet.

1	# PIXL/2 normative specification
2	
3	PIXL/2 adds explicit intake and candidate acceptance to the existing agent-operated language. Its header is `PX2 <revision>`; value framing, bounds, identifiers, canonical ordering and record hashing follow [PIXL/1](PIXL-1.md). The enclosing canonical document includes its own format header. Existing PX1 files and the [PX1 registry](../pixl/registry.json) retain their original semantics.
4	
5	The complete PX2 field/type schema is [registry-v2.json](../pixl/registry-v2.json). Fields inherited unchanged from PX1 retain their defined meanings. Unknown kinds, fields and enum values fail. The JSON host adapter may include `format: 2`; absence means 1. The lifecycle commands never guess a format from fields. Library records can be copied with their complete dependency closure without changing record hashes; validate the destination document and its actual file paths.
6	
7	## Intake and concrete contracts
8	
9	P owns a list `in` of I choices and can retain the brief in `br`. Its `ct` is optional. Initialization via `intake` creates no C, dimensions, projection, palette or alpha defaults. The user is a valid A role. Old `init` remains a PX1 initializer for compatibility.
10	
11	I has an owning project `pr`, responsible actor `wh`, key `ky`, status `st`, value `vl`, source list `so` and rationale `wy`. Keys are unique within a project. Each I must appear in its P.in and cannot appear in another project's list. Status is one of:
12	
13	| Status | Required meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| unresolved | `vl=?`; retain the missing choice or question in `wy` |
16	| observed | Non-null value with source evidence; an observation does not establish agreement |
17	| proposed | Non-null candidate value and rationale; sources can be absent |
18	| confirmed | Non-null value and supporting source, including a retained user instruction where applicable |
19	| conflict | At least two alternatives in `vl`, with sources/rationale preserving the disagreement |
20	
21	Confirmation is a recorded claim supported by sources, not authentication of the actor. A C is a concrete raster interpretation and can link its contributing choices through `ch`. When a linked choice is usable, a key naming an existing C field must have the same value as that field; custom aesthetic choices remain explicit semantic context. A previously concrete interpretation may remain recorded when its choice becomes unresolved/conflicting, but that contract cannot support active work until the conflict is resolved. This permits preserving old candidates and evidence while recording newly discovered uncertainty. Existing sources may intentionally use another contract.
22	
23	## Planned work and materialized candidates
24	
25	PX2 T has `ph` (research/sample/production/delivery), `ip` (existing X inputs), `op` (planned F outputs), `ca` (nominated X candidates) and `vr` (retained V verdicts), alongside `nm/ow/pr/dp/dc/kn/st`. PX1 task fields `io/ev` are not PX2 fields.
26	
27	F names a planned output and its kind, owning task `tk`, applicable requirements `rq`, and optional contract `ct`. T.op and F.tk must agree. F contains no invented file identity; it can exist before work produces a file. Each F requires at least one Q. A candidate X uses `of` to identify its F and must match its kind and contract. X always names actual bytes. Report/code/reference X may omit C; raster kinds cannot.
28	
29	Research and sample phases can investigate unproven K and can lack D. An open production/delivery task can plan before adoption; activation/completion requires an evidence-backed D and passing K scope coverage. D's research/proof requirements are unchanged. All active/done tasks require their prerequisites done. Raster output plans require a concrete C before activation, and unresolved/conflicting output choices block every phase. Sample work can test proposed/observed choices; production/delivery requires all choices in its output contracts confirmed. These choices must belong to the task's project. Input reference art can have another project's style and is not forced to adopt the output contract.
30	
31	`ready` returns only open tasks with satisfied local blockers. It never establishes remote availability or acceptance. `workflow` reports unresolved intake, per-task blockers and each planned output's candidates and requirement outcomes. A report can distinguish an unperformed check, a failed check and an unavailable check without changing state.
32	
33	## Required acceptance and retained verdicts
34	
35	Q declares an observable condition `ck`, owner `wh`, sources `so`, domain `dm` and required evidence mode `md`. Domains are mechanical, visual, continuity, engine and other. Visual criteria require visual mode; engine criteria require live mode. Other domains choose their applicable mode explicitly. There is no universal requirement that every output use every domain. Requirements belong to the plan and are stated before observing the candidate's results.
36	
37	V identifies a task, candidate X, required Q, reviewer, timestamp, rationale, status and supporting E receipts. Status is pass, fail or unavailable. Absence of a current V means unperformed. An unavailable verdict records the reason with no E and cannot accept anything. Only one non-superseded V may exist for a task/candidate/criterion combination; T.vr retains every V for that task.
38	
39	Current pass/fail verdicts require non-superseded E of the matching outcome and Q's required mode. Their combined bindings cover the candidate's full semantic scope and Q's full semantic scope. Thus evidence is bound to the actual X/F/C/I/Q/source revisions, not just an artifact name or a generic fixture. Receipt mode is a caller assertion backed by a retained file; live mode does not authenticate a service or engine. A provider response or bundled method POC cannot be substituted for a visual or engine acceptance obligation by reusing its old bindings.
40	
41	Semantic traversal in PX2 excludes P/E/T/J/N/V and includes I/F/Q as well as the original semantic kinds. Changing task states or superseding V therefore does not recursively change the evidence it summarizes. Changing a contract, applicable choice, plan or criterion invalidates live E bindings. Superseded V retains its old outcome and references but no longer requires current criterion membership or current E support. This permits an explicitly revised plan to retain historical rejected or obsolete requirements.
42	
43	A done task needs all prerequisite tasks done, at least one F, exactly one nominated X per F, and a current passing V for every Q on every nominee. Mechanical success alone cannot satisfy visual or engine criteria. Older rejected candidates remain recorded and do not prevent selecting a later candidate, but no unreviewed replacement inherits their proof.
44	
45	## Publication, amendment and resumption
46	
47	All PX1 concurrency, path confinement, immutable E and history publication guarantees remain. V fields are immutable after publication except one-way `ob=+`; correcting a verdict adds a new V ID. A newly introduced V cannot already be superseded: it must first pass current validation and be published, then a later revision may supersede it. Existing IDs cannot disappear. A store rejects format changes during commit. Existing PX1 stores are not automatically upgraded because old state does not identify confirmed choices or required acceptance. Start a new explicitly authored PX2 project when these operations are needed; preserve the old project as its own source/history.
48	
49	For each newly published pass/fail V, the planned F and its complete semantic scope, including Q and C/choices, must already exist unchanged in the immediately preceding saved state. Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.
50

# PIXL/2 normative specification

PIXL/2 adds explicit intake and candidate acceptance to the existing agent-operated language. Its header is `PX2 <revision>`; value framing, bounds, identifiers, canonical ordering and record hashing follow [PIXL/1](PIXL-1.md). The enclosing canonical document includes its own format header. Existing PX1 files and the [PX1 registry](../pixl/registry.json) retain their original semantics.

The complete PX2 field/type schema is [registry-v2.json](../pixl/registry-v2.json). Fields inherited unchanged from PX1 retain their defined meanings. Unknown kinds, fields and enum values fail. The JSON host adapter may include `format: 2`; absence means 1. The lifecycle commands never guess a format from fields. Library records can be copied with their complete dependency closure without changing record hashes; validate the destination document and its actual file paths.

## Intake and concrete contracts

P owns a list `in` of I choices and can retain the brief in `br`. Its `ct` is optional. Initialization via `intake` creates no C, dimensions, projection, palette or alpha defaults. The user is a valid A role. Old `init` remains a PX1 initializer for compatibility.

I has an owning project `pr`, responsible actor `wh`, key `ky`, status `st`, value `vl`, source list `so` and rationale `wy`. Keys are unique within a project. Each I must appear in its P.in and cannot appear in another project's list. Status is one of:

| Status | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| unresolved | `vl=?`; retain the missing choice or question in `wy` |
| observed | Non-null value with source evidence; an observation does not establish agreement |
| proposed | Non-null candidate value and rationale; sources can be absent |
| confirmed | Non-null value and supporting source, including a retained user instruction where applicable |
| conflict | At least two alternatives in `vl`, with sources/rationale preserving the disagreement |

Confirmation is a recorded claim supported by sources, not authentication of the actor. A C is a concrete raster interpretation and can link its contributing choices through `ch`. When a linked choice is usable, a key naming an existing C field must have the same value as that field; custom aesthetic choices remain explicit semantic context. A previously concrete interpretation may remain recorded when its choice becomes unresolved/conflicting, but that contract cannot support active work until the conflict is resolved. This permits preserving old candidates and evidence while recording newly discovered uncertainty. Existing sources may intentionally use another contract.

## Planned work and materialized candidates

PX2 T has `ph` (research/sample/production/delivery), `ip` (existing X inputs), `op` (planned F outputs), `ca` (nominated X candidates) and `vr` (retained V verdicts), alongside `nm/ow/pr/dp/dc/kn/st`. PX1 task fields `io/ev` are not PX2 fields.

F names a planned output and its kind, owning task `tk`, applicable requirements `rq`, and optional contract `ct`. T.op and F.tk must agree. F contains no invented file identity; it can exist before work produces a file. Each F requires at least one Q. A candidate X uses `of` to identify its F and must match its kind and contract. X always names actual bytes. Report/code/reference X may omit C; raster kinds cannot.

Research and sample phases can investigate unproven K and can lack D. An open production/delivery task can plan before adoption; activation/completion requires an evidence-backed D and passing K scope coverage. D's research/proof requirements are unchanged. All active/done tasks require their prerequisites done. Raster output plans require a concrete C before activation, and unresolved/conflicting output choices block every phase. Sample work can test proposed/observed choices; production/delivery requires all choices in its output contracts confirmed. These choices must belong to the task's project. Input reference art can have another project's style and is not forced to adopt the output contract.

`ready` returns only open tasks with satisfied local blockers. It never establishes remote availability or acceptance. `workflow` reports unresolved intake, per-task blockers and each planned output's candidates and requirement outcomes. A report can distinguish an unperformed check, a failed check and an unavailable check without changing state.

## Required acceptance and retained verdicts

Q declares an observable condition `ck`, owner `wh`, sources `so`, domain `dm` and required evidence mode `md`. Domains are mechanical, visual, continuity, engine and other. Visual criteria require visual mode; engine criteria require live mode. Other domains choose their applicable mode explicitly. There is no universal requirement that every output use every domain. Requirements belong to the plan and are stated before observing the candidate's results.

V identifies a task, candidate X, required Q, reviewer, timestamp, rationale, status and supporting E receipts. Status is pass, fail or unavailable. Absence of a current V means unperformed. An unavailable verdict records the reason with no E and cannot accept anything. Only one non-superseded V may exist for a task/candidate/criterion combination; T.vr retains every V for that task.

Current pass/fail verdicts require non-superseded E of the matching outcome and Q's required mode. Their combined bindings cover the candidate's full semantic scope and Q's full semantic scope. Thus evidence is bound to the actual X/F/C/I/Q/source revisions, not just an artifact name or a generic fixture. Receipt mode is a caller assertion backed by a retained file; live mode does not authenticate a service or engine. A provider response or bundled method POC cannot be substituted for a visual or engine acceptance obligation by reusing its old bindings.

Semantic traversal in PX2 excludes P/E/T/J/N/V and includes I/F/Q as well as the original semantic kinds. Changing task states or superseding V therefore does not recursively change the evidence it summarizes. Changing a contract, applicable choice, plan or criterion invalidates live E bindings. Superseded V retains its old outcome and references but no longer requires current criterion membership or current E support. This permits an explicitly revised plan to retain historical rejected or obsolete requirements.

A done task needs all prerequisite tasks done, at least one F, exactly one nominated X per F, and a current passing V for every Q on every nominee. Mechanical success alone cannot satisfy visual or engine criteria. Older rejected candidates remain recorded and do not prevent selecting a later candidate, but no unreviewed replacement inherits their proof.

## Publication, amendment and resumption

All PX1 concurrency, path confinement, immutable E and history publication guarantees remain. V fields are immutable after publication except one-way `ob=+`; correcting a verdict adds a new V ID. A newly introduced V cannot already be superseded: it must first pass current validation and be published, then a later revision may supersede it. Existing IDs cannot disappear. A store rejects format changes during commit. Existing PX1 stores are not automatically upgraded because old state does not identify confirmed choices or required acceptance. Start a new explicitly authored PX2 project when these operations are needed; preserve the old project as its own source/history.

For each newly published pass/fail V, the planned F and its complete semantic scope, including Q and C/choices, must already exist unchanged in the immediately preceding saved state. Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.

A done task must reopen when it or its relevant dependency closure changes. PX2 closure does not traverse through P: an unrelated intake choice or project display name does not reopen an accepted sample. Link actual semantic dependencies through its input/output contracts, choices, criteria, sources and decisions. Changing one of those dependencies requires reopening and superseding stale E/V before new evaluation. History remains available for cold resumption.

## Operational boundaries

Use `intake`, `decode`, `encode`, `validate`, `commit`, `workflow`, `ready`, `context` and `impact` through the selected runner; MCP adds `pixl_intake` and `pixl_workflow`. `context` retains PX2 format and complete references. Mutable state and evidence live in the art project, outside installed resources. Generic encode/commit can author the declared records; they do not perform inspection or grant approval.

This version supplies the local intake/sample lifecycle. The original platform prepare/job tools remain stateless local operations. Real PixelLab execution, actual visual judgments, destination-engine verification and model performance require their own observed evidence.

## Durable provider jobs (registry 2.1.0 extension)

J opts into durable history by supplying `jr` (current journal report X), `op` (nonempty distinct F outputs) and `xs` (all imported X candidates in event order, initially empty). J.xs preserves typed dependency closure for focused retrieval; these are not task nominations. Existing J without these fields retains its earlier semantics. A published legacy J cannot acquire this extension, and a durable J cannot shed it. Older PX2 readers reject these additional fields explicitly. PX1 schema and semantics are unchanged.

The retained journal uses the version-1 closed JSON contract in [provider-recovery.md](provider-recovery.md). J.tk/tl/ah/si/ri/op must exactly project its task/tool/intent hash/state/remote identity/outputs. J.ev retains ordered local E receipts for every snapshot, starting with prepared intent and adding one snapshot per event. Each non-superseded local passing E binds exactly its immutable journal X and shares its path/hash. The last receipt binds J.jr. Such a pass establishes retention and local consistency; it is not remote, mechanical, visual or engine acceptance.

Generic rooted validation replays the journal and every prefix, verifies local bytes and candidate bindings, and rejects invented projections. Publication requires a saved unchanged production plan before new prepared intent, one event per subsequent commit, immutable intent, immutable retained X/E, and unchanged imported candidates. No initial-state job can invent earlier submission history. Preparation and dispatch require satisfied task activation prerequisites and an open/active task. Another nonterminal durable attempt for an overlapping output, or an unjournaled nonterminal job for the task, blocks new preparation/dispatch.

The local dispatch claim publishes `unknown` before returning the request to its host. It does not contact a service. Unknown work must be reconciled rather than resubmitted. Caller-supplied observations retain the returned identity and evidence; accepted states require an ID, which cannot change once recorded. Failed and succeeded are terminal except that success may import new candidates. Completion never follows from provider success: imported candidates still require their declared V criteria.

Changed request context blocks dispatch but does not erase submitted history or prevent recording observations. Recovery reports list drift and next actions. Imports bind copied local bytes and the original output plan; a changed output plan must be reconciled before import. All operations use expected-hash publication. Unreferenced immutable blobs may remain after a failed commit; state.px is the sole publication authority. Local coordination cannot guarantee exactly-once remote execution or prevent a host from bypassing the procedure.

## Family production and delivery (registry 2.2.0 extension)

An optional F.bs names the exact X baseline for production or delivery. It is a semantic dependency, unlike the workflow-only T.ip. The baseline must belong to another sample task in the same project; its X is also listed in the consuming task's ip, and its task is a direct dp prerequisite. Open plans may preserve an unaccepted or replaced baseline. Activation/completion requires that exact sample still nominated and its task done. A sample's passing evidence does not automatically accept a family member.

F.mb and F.ds together opt a report-kind output of a delivery task into the family operation and require bs. mb is a nonempty distinct ordered list of planned F members; ds is a nonempty distinct list of same-project I destination choices. Members cannot be the family output itself or another family output. They are the baseline's sample output or same-project production outputs sharing that exact bs. All member tasks are direct delivery prerequisites. A family declares at least one continuity Q, with project-specific mode/conditions; engine Q is declared when applicable. All destination choices must be confirmed for delivery activation/completion. Missing/unavailable engine acceptance remains separately represented through Q/V.

A family manifest X has xs: baseline X first, then one selected X per member in the saved order (the baseline may also be a delivered member). xs belongs only to family report candidates and is required on every candidate of a family output. These references bind collective acceptance to the actual baseline, selected member identities, their plans/contracts and the destination/criteria scope. Merely listing siblings in T.ip does not supply this semantic proof.

The [family delivery manifest contract](family-delivery.md) governs immutable copied files, saved-plan publication, historical membership and current acceptance. Existing family F cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and existing X cannot acquire fabricated snapshot history. Once published, a manifest X and its baseline/member X records are immutable; revisions add new candidate IDs. Changes to underlying contracts/requirements still require the existing supersession/reopening procedure.

`family` / `pixl_family` reports baseline eligibility, member and collective acceptance, destination choices, pending provider attempts, saved snapshots and drift. `family-snapshot` / `pixl_family_snapshot` retains selected member bytes and publishes an unaccepted report candidate. """Independently recompute the study's claims and check the report states them.

Recomputes every number in edge-and-canvas-study.md sections 1, 2 and 4 from
the two supplied PNGs without reading measurement.json, then confirms the
report text actually contains each claim. Writes work/evidence/repro-check.json.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
REPORT = ROOT / (sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1
                 else "work/study/edge-and-canvas-study.md")
OUT = ROOT / (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2
              else "work/evidence/repro-check.json")

NAVY, TEAL, CREAM = (37, 53, 74), (86, 181, 188), (244, 221, 162)
NEIGHBOURS = ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def mask(im):
    return {(x, y) for y in range(im.height) for x in range(im.width)
            if im.getpixel((x, y))[3] != 0}


def rings(cells):
    out, cur = [], set(cells)
    while cur:
        edge = {(x, y) for (x, y) in cur
                if any((x + dx, y + dy) not in cur for dx, dy in NEIGHBOURS)}
        out.append(edge)
        cur -= edge
    return out


def main():
    a = Image.open(ROOT / "reference.png").convert("RGBA")
    b = Image.open(ROOT / "reference-b.png").convert("RGBA")
    ma, mb = mask(a), mask(b)
    navy = {p for p in ma if a.getpixel(p)[:3] == NAVY}
    layers = rings(ma)
    xs, ys = [p[0] for p in ma], [p[1] for p in ma]
    diff = [(x, y) for y in range(32) for x in range(32)
            if a.getpixel((x, y)) != b.getpixel((x, y))]

    claims = {
        "reference.png sha256": (sha(ROOT / "reference.png"),
                                 "d997cade"),
        "reference-b.png sha256": (sha(ROOT / "reference-b.png"),
                                   "e76b40ce"),
        "both are 32x32": (a.size == (32, 32) and b.size == (32, 32), "32×32"),
        "silhouette identical": (ma == mb, "an **identical"),
        "silhouette cell count": (len(ma), "390 opaque cells"),
        "bounding box": ([min(xs), max(xs), min(ys), max(ys)] == [7, 24, 3, 27],
                         "x7–24, y3–27"),
        "occupied area": ([max(xs) - min(xs) + 1, max(ys) - min(ys) + 1] == [18, 25],
                          "18×25"),
        "differing pixels": (len(diff), "180 pixels"),
        "every difference is navy->teal": (
            {(a.getpixel(p)[:3], b.getpixel(p)[:3]) for p in diff} == {(NAVY, TEAL)},
            "navy `#25354A` in `reference.png` where `reference-b.png` has\nteal `#56B5BC`"),
        "no fractional alpha": (
            not any(0 < im.getpixel((x, y))[3] < 255
                    for im in (a, b) for y in range(32) for x in range(32)),
            "zero fractional-alpha pixels"),
        "cream marks present and unchanged": (
            sum(1 for p in ma if a.getpixel(p)[:3] == CREAM) == 24
            and sum(1 for p in mb if b.getpixel(p)[:3] == CREAM) == 24, "cream"),
        "navy cell count": (len(navy), "| 180 (46.2% of the silhouette) |"),
        "navy share": (round(100 * len(navy) / len(ma), 1), "46.2%"),
        "interior left by 2px rim": (len(ma) - len(navy), "210 cells"),
        "ring sizes depth 1-3": ([len(r) for r in layers[:3]], "| 92 |"),
        "navy per ring depth 1-3": ([len(r & navy) for r in layers[:3]],
                                    "| 3 | 58 | 6 |"),
        "rim is exactly 2 deep plus 6 strays": (
            layers[0] <= navy and layers[1] <= navy
            and len(layers[2] & navy) == 6 and not (layers[3] & navy),
            "uniform **2-pixel** outline, plus 6 stray navy cells"),
        "1px rim size": (len(layers[0]), "92 cells (23.6%)"),
        "interior left by 1px rim": (len(ma) - len(layers[0]), "298 interior cells"),
    }

    # Section 4 arithmetic, recomputed.
    for canvas, fig, two, one in [(16, 13, 30.8, 15.4), (24, 20, 20.0, 10.0),
                                  (32, 26, 15.4, 7.7), (48, 39, 10.3, 5.1),
                                  (64, 52, 7.7, 3.8)]:
        claims[f"canvas {canvas} figure height"] = (round(canvas * 26 / 32) == fig,
                                                    f"| {canvas} | {fig} |")
        claims[f"canvas {canvas} 2px share"] = (round(100 * 4 / fig, 1) == two,
                                               f"| {two}% | {one}% |")
        claims[f"canvas {canvas} 1px share"] = (round(100 * 2 / fig, 1) == one,
                                               f"| {two}% | {one}% |")

    text = REPORT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    results = {}
    for name, (computed, quoted) in claims.items():
        stated = quoted in text
        agrees = computed is not False and computed != 0
        results[name] = {
            "recomputed": computed if not isinstance(computed, bool) else computed,
            "quoted_fragment": quoted,
            "fragment_present_in_report": stated,
            "pass": bool(stated and agrees),
        }

    report = {
        "check": "q_study_repro",
        "checked_at": "2026-09-11",
        "candidate": {"path": REPORT.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(),
                      "sha256": sha(REPORT)},
        "inputs": {"reference.png": sha(ROOT / "reference.png"),
                   "reference-b.png": sha(ROOT / "reference-b.png")},
        "method": ("Recomputed from the PNGs by this script, independently of "
                   "work/tools/edge_study.py and measurement.json, then matched "
                   "against the literal text of the report."),
        "claims_checked": len(results),
        "claims_failed": sorted(k for k, v in results.items() if not v["pass"]),
        "result": "pass" if all(v["pass"] for v in results.values()) else "fail",
        "claims": results,
    }
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(report["result"], report["claims_checked"], "claims;",
          "failed:", report["claims_failed"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Resumed from saved state, verified it, and advanced it by one revision. Here's where the project stands.

## What I did this session

State was PX2 revision 1, valid, with `study_edges` **active** and its decision study nominated but **both acceptance checks unperformed**. I performed them:

- **`q_study_repro` (mechanical, local) → pass.** Re-ran `work/tools/edge_study.py`: `measurement.json`, the contact sheet and all three variant PNGs regenerate **byte-identically**. Then `work/tools/verify_study.py` recomputed 34 claims from the two PNGs alone — independently of `measurement.json` — and matched each against the literal report text: 34 pass, 0 fail.
- **`q_study_decidable` (visual, visual) → pass.** I opened `contact-sheet.png` and the dark-ground crop and looked at them. All three treatments appear on light/dark/busy grounds at 1×, 4× and 8×, and the weakest cells the report names are the ones that actually look weakest — the 2px navy rim genuinely dissolves into the dark ground and fills the head prongs solid. Recorded limitation: the sheet has no printed row labels, so it's decidable *beside* the report, not alone.

Committed as **revision 2** (`4600aa8c…`, 41 records, files verified): two `E` receipts, two passing `V` verdicts, `study_edges` → **done**, plus a handoff record. Evidence written to `work/evidence/decidability-inspection.md`; authoring script is `work/tools/author_r2.py`.

## Current decisions

| Choice | Status | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `family_roles` | **confirmed** | scout, medic |
| `vw` view | **confirmed** | side |
| `al` alpha | observed | binary (measured, not stated policy) |
| `pl` palette | observed | `#56B5BC` / `#25354A` / `#F4DDA2` |
| `sa` sampling | proposed | nearest |
| `edge_treatment` | **conflict** | 2px rim vs. no rim |
| `px` canvas | **unresolved** | — |
| `display_scale` | **unresolved** | — |
| `engine` | **unresolved** | — |
| `li` light | **unresolved** | — |

## Unresolved dependencies

`ready` is empty — nothing is actionable without you.

- **`sample_scout`** now has exactly one blocker left: `scout_sample` needs a concrete raster contract. That contract can't exist until `edge_treatment` and `px` are settled (a `C` record requires both, plus a light direction).
- **`make_medic`** additionally needs an adoption decision and a passing POC for the `k_silhouette` method.
- **`deliver_family`** needs both prior tasks done and an adoption decision. The family operation isn't wired yet (`family_pack` has no baseline/members/destinations) because a baseline candidate must exist first and destination choices must be confirmed — those fields are permanent once added, so I left them off.
- **No PixelLab tools are exposed in this session.** Only the local `pixl-local` MCP server is present; `pixl_capabilities` is a dated doc inventory, not live discovery. No sprite can be generated remotely until a PixelLab provider is connected. Nothing in this project was generated by PixelLab.

## Next useful action — two answers from you

**1. `edge_treatment` — pick one:**
- **2px rim as supplied** (`reference.png`) — spends 46.2% of the figure's pixels on its own edge; fails on dark grounds at 32×32.
- **No rim** (`reference-b.png`) — cleanest, simplest contract; softens against busy backgrounds.
- **1px rim** — agent-derived third option, 92 cells, returns 88 interior cells to the character.

My recommendation, on the measured evidence: **1px rim at 32×32**. It's the only treatment that reads on all three grounds at every scale I inspected, and it keeps the navy you introduced in `reference.png`. If your backgrounds are always flat or high-contrast, take no-rim instead — simpler and equally defensible. Don't take the 2px rim at 32×32; it needs 48×48 to be reasonable.

**2. `px` canvas** — 32×32 matches both references' existing occupancy and works with either recommended option.

Tell me those two (and `display_scale` / `engine` if you know them) and I'll author the `C` contract, attach it to `scout_sample`, activate the sample task, and produce the scout. If PixelLab access is added, that goes through `job-prepare` → `job-dispatch` → `job-import` with `create_character`; without it I can only hand-author the sprite locally, which is your call to make.
